The SDK's outer build sets `$(TargetFrameworks)` → dispatches the inner build which sets `$(TargetFramework)`, but `.props` files are imported *before* the SDK's TFM-dispatch logic runs. This condition **never evaluates to true**, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is silently never set.

**Fix:** Move TFM-conditional property logic to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is imported *after* the SDK sets `$(TargetFramework)`:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E2 — Property defaults in `.targets` silently override project-level values

**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 7–10  
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported *after* the project file. MSBuild uses last-write-wins for properties, so these values **unconditionally override** any project-level settings. Specifically, `LibB.csproj` line 13 sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`, but this `.targets` file silently reverts it to `true`. LibB's developers have no idea their opt-out is ignored.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` with conditional defaults so projects can override them:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E3 — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 13–15  
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Two issues here:**

1. **Overwrites, not appends:** This replaces `DefineConstants` entirely, killing the SDK-provided `DEBUG` and `TRACE` constants. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working.

2. **Unquoted condition:** `$(Configuration) == Debug` is missing quotes around both sides. If `$(Configuration)` is ever empty, this evaluates to ` == Debug` which is a malformed expression. MSBuild may tolerate this today but it's fragile and violates best practices.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
  <DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E4 — F# compilation order is wrong (will fail to compile)

**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9  
```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** F# is **compilation-order-sensitive** — files can only reference types/modules from files listed *above* them. `Services.fs` (line 7) opens `BrokenOrder.Domain` (defined in `Domain.fs`, line 8), but `Domain.fs` appears *after* `Services.fs`. This will produce a compile error like `FS0039: The namespace or module 'BrokenOrder.Domain' is not defined`.

Compare with the correct order in `fsharp/OrderService/OrderService.fsproj`:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />    <!-- types defined first -->
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />  <!-- depends on Domain -->
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />   <!-- depends on both -->
```

**Fix:** Reorder to match the dependency chain:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

---

### 🔴 E5 — `PublishOnBuild` re-invokes same project, causing double build and potential file race

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45  
```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This uses the `<MSBuild>` task to call back into the *same* project with an extra global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). MSBuild treats this as a **distinct project instance** (same path, different global properties), which triggers a full re-evaluation and re-execution. Both instances write to the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, creating a race condition on output files. In parallel builds (`-m`), this can cause intermittent `IOException` failures.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish in the same project instance, with a guard property to prevent recursion:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishAfterBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>

<Target Name="PublishAfterBuild"
        Condition="'$(_IsPublishing)' != 'true'"
        DependsOnTargets="Publish" />
```

## 🟡 Warnings

### 🟡 W1 — Analyzer package leaks to downstream consumers

**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 16–18  
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, this analyzer package flows transitively to any project that references LibA or LibB via `<ProjectReference>`. Downstream consumers will be forced to run StyleCop analysis even if they don't want it.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

### 🟡 W2 — Hardcoded Windows-only `OutputPath`

**Files:** `LibA/LibA.csproj` line 7 and `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 7  
```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** Absolute Windows paths break builds on macOS/Linux and tie the project to a specific machine's directory structure. This path also doesn't include `$(Configuration)` or `$(TargetFramework)`, so Debug and Release builds overwrite each other.

**Fix:** Use relative, cross-platform paths with configuration segmentation:
```xml
<OutputPath>bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\</OutputPath>
```
Or remove entirely — the SDK default (`bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\`) is usually correct.

---

### 🟡 W3 — Duplicate Compile item (CS2002 warning risk)

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 21–23  
```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```

**Problem:** In an SDK-style project, `*.cs` files are automatically included via implicit globbing. The explicit `<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />` creates a **duplicate** entry, which produces warning `CS2002: Source file 'Class1.cs' specified multiple times`. The `Update` should be used alone (without the `Include`) to add metadata to the auto-globbed item.

**Fix:**
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### 🟡 W4 — Legacy `<Reference>` with HintPath instead of `PackageReference`

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–29  
```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-era assembly reference pointing to a `packages\` folder. In an SDK-style project, this is incorrect — the `packages\` folder won't exist unless manually created, so this reference will fail to resolve. Even if the DLL is present, it targets `net6.0` while the project targets `net8.0`, which is a TFM mismatch.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 🟡 W5 — `LibB.csproj` TreatWarningsAsErrors opt-out is silently ignored

**File:** `LibB/LibB.csproj`, line 13  
```xml
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
```

**Problem:** This appears intentional but has **no effect** because `Directory.Build.targets` (imported after this file) unconditionally sets `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`, overriding this value. Developers maintaining LibB will believe warnings aren't errors when they actually are. This is a consequence of the issue in **E2** above.

**Fix:** Resolve E2 by moving the default to `.props` with a condition, and this opt-out will work as intended.

### 🔵 S1 — Adopt Central Package Management (CPM)

Package versions are scattered across `Directory.Build.props` and `LibA.csproj`. With only two packages currently this is manageable, but as the solution grows, version drift becomes a risk.

**Suggestion:** Create a `Directory.Packages.props` file:
```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageVersion Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```
Then remove `Version=` from individual `<PackageReference>` items.

### 🔵 S2 — `PrintVersion` target has no `Inputs`/`Outputs`

**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 32–34  
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

This target runs on every build because it has no `Inputs`/`Outputs` for incremental skip. For a simple echo this is harmless, but it sets a bad precedent. If this evolves into something more expensive, it will slow every incremental build.
